# RapidTally Ace v0.1.0 — Phase 0 (read-path spike)

First public release of **RapidTally Ace** (formerly codenamed *Bookwright*) —
an independent, clean-room, cross-platform accounting suite. This is the
**phase-0 scaffold**: a structural probe for QuickBooks Desktop database files
plus full multi-platform release engineering. It is **not** yet an accounting
application.

## What's inside

- `rapidtally-format` — clean-room probe library: ASCII marker scan
  (`SQL Anywhere` / `Sybase` / `Intuit` / `QuickBooks`), candidate page-size
  analysis, per-region Shannon-entropy mapping, hex dump, and a minimal C ABI
  (`rtace_version`, `rtace_probe_buffer`) for future Kotlin/JNI and Qt
  embedding.
- `rapidtally-ace` — CLI front end (`rapidtally-ace inspect <file>`).
- Clean-room engineering protocol, roadmap with G0/G1 legal & fidelity gates,
  platform docs (`docs/`).
- Rust toolchain pinned to **1.77.2** — the last release that supports
  Windows 7.

## Install notes

- **Windows 7+:** the C runtime is statically linked — no Visual C++
  redistributable needed. Unzip and run
  `rapidtally-ace.exe inspect <file>`.
- **macOS Catalina+:** binaries are ad-hoc signed; if Gatekeeper complains,
  run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine rapidtally-ace` or right-click → Open.
- **Linux Mint / Debian:** the static binary has zero runtime dependencies,
  or install the `.deb`: `sudo apt install ./rapidtally-ace_0.1.0_amd64.deb`.
- **Flatpak:** `flatpak install --user ./RapidTallyAce-0.1.0-x86_64.flatpak`
  then `flatpak run com.rapidtallyace.RapidTallyAce inspect <file>`.
- **Android:** phase-0 validation artifacts (CLI binary + JNI `.so`) proving
  the NDK toolchain for the future Kotlin/Compose shell — not yet a
  user-facing app.

Verify your download against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
